title: Token Probability
shortDefinition: The likelihood an LLM assigns to each possible next word during generation.
definition: Token probability is the likelihood an LLM internally assigns to each possible next token (word or word-piece) at each step of generating its response — the model is constantly calculating, 'given everything so far, how likely is each possible next token,' and these probabilities (sometimes accessible via the API as 'log probabilities' or 'logprobs') can be examined as a signal about the model's internal certainty or uncertainty at each point in its generated output. Token probability data offers a more granular signal than an overall response-level confidence score, useful for diagnosing specifically where in a response the model was uncertain.

sections.title: How token probability can reveal model uncertainty
sections.description: Token-level probability reveals which parts of a response the model was uncertain about.

content.text: When an LLM generates each token, it's selecting from a probability distribution over its entire vocabulary — if the model assigns high probability to one clearly dominant token, it suggests relative confidence at that point; if probability is spread more evenly across several plausible alternative tokens, it suggests genuine uncertainty about what should come next. This token-level granularity can reveal specifically which part of a longer response the model was least certain about, distinct from an overall single confidence score for the entire response, which can mask uncertainty concentrated in just one problematic section.

items: High probability — clear dominant token suggests confidence.
Spread probability — several plausible alternatives suggest uncertainty.
Granular insight — reveals where in a long response uncertainty lies.
Overall scores mask issues — single confidence scores hide concentrated uncertainty.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Token probability offers granular visibility into uncertainty — an overall confident-sounding response can hide uncertainty concentrated in just one problematic section.

sections.title: Practical applications of token probability analysis

content.text: Token probability data can be used to flag specific spans of a generated response for additional scrutiny (rather than treating the entire response uniformly), inform more sophisticated confidence scoring that weighs token-level uncertainty rather than relying solely on a model's self-reported overall confidence, and in some research contexts, help detect potential hallucination by identifying unusually low-probability token sequences that may indicate the model is generating less grounded, more speculative content at that specific point.

items: Targeted review — flag specific spans for scrutiny.
Sophisticated confidence — token-level weighting of uncertainty.
Hallucination detection — unusually low-probability sequences.
Speculative content identification — less grounded generation.

sections.title: Limitations and risks of token probability analysis

content.text: Token probability analysis has limitations. It adds implementation complexity and may increase latency for processing. Access to token probability data varies by provider and may not be available for all models. Token probability is not a perfect uncertainty signal — models can be confidently wrong with high-probability tokens, and low-probability tokens don't always indicate errors. The technique requires careful calibration and interpretation, and for many applications, simpler overall confidence scoring provides sufficient value without the added complexity.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about token probability

items.question: Is token probability the same as the overall confidence score for a response?
items.answer: No — an overall confidence score typically represents the entire response; token probability provides much more granular, per-token data that can reveal uncertainty concentrated in just one specific section of a longer response.

items.question: Can token probability reliably detect hallucination?
items.answer: It's one useful signal — unusually low-probability token sequences can correlate with less grounded, more speculative content — but it's not a fully reliable standalone hallucination detector; ClickMasters typically combines it with RAG grounding and other techniques rather than relying on it alone.

items.question: Do all LLM providers give developers access to token probability data?
items.answer: Access varies by provider and can change over time; ClickMasters confirms current capabilities for your specific provider during Discovery.

items.question: Is this technique relevant for short responses, or mainly long-form content?
items.answer: It's most valuable for longer, more complex generated content where uncertainty in one specific section might otherwise be masked by an overall confident-sounding response; shorter responses may not benefit as much from this granularity.

items.question: How long does implementing token-probability-aware analysis take?
items.answer: 6–16 weeks depending on the specific application — confidence scoring, content flagging, or research-oriented hallucination detection.

items.question: Should every AI application use token probability analysis?
items.answer: No, this is a specialized technique most valuable for high-stakes, long-form generated content; many applications are adequately served by simpler overall confidence scoring approaches.

items.question: What are log probabilities (logprobs) in LLM APIs?
items.answer: Log probabilities are the logarithmic transform of token probabilities — they provide numerical stability and are often exposed by LLM APIs. They can be used to calculate probability values or compare confidence across tokens.

items.question: How does token probability differ from temperature?
items.answer: Temperature controls how much the model's probability distribution is sharpened or flattened during sampling — higher temperature flattens the distribution, making less probable tokens more likely. Token probability is the raw likelihood before temperature is applied.

items.question: Can token probability be used for token-level uncertainty visualization?
items.answer: Yes — token probability can be visualized to show which parts of a generated response the model was most and least certain about. This is useful for debugging and quality analysis.

items.question: Is token probability available for all LLM models?
items.answer: Availability depends on the provider and model version. Some providers expose it via API parameters; others do not. ClickMasters confirms availability during provider selection.
